---
applyTo: "release-copilot/src/release_agent/tools/**/*.py,src/release_agent/tools/**/*.py"
---
# Tool layer (GitHub, BigQuery, git)

These modules are the source of truth for every fact the portal shows. The chat
model only chooses which tool to call.

- **Return, don't raise, for expected failures.** Tools return a dict (or a
  JSON string that `gh_tools.coerce_result` turns into one) with `ok` and a
  human `note`/`error`. A string starting `ERROR` is treated as a failure.
- **GitHub access** goes through `_common._get_github_client()` and
  `active_deploy_repo()`. Never build a client from a raw token here: the
  per-thread connected PAT is resolved for you (`session_creds.py`).
- **Every commit, PR title and merge** uses `attribution.py`:
  `attribution.titled(...)` for PR titles, `attribution.commit_message(...)` for
  commit messages, `attribution.with_trailer(...)` for PR bodies,
  `**attribution.author_kwargs()` on file writes, and
  `**attribution.merge_kwargs(pr)` on merges. Do not add anything else to the
  files you write (no "updated_by" stamps); keep a file's trailing newline.
- **UAT deploy chain** (`promotion.py`): an override of `uat/deployment.json`,
  one at a time (`uat_deploy_blocker`, `_claim_uat_deploy`). UAT changes always
  flow via SIT: the portal merges into SIT only and shows the repository's own
  SIT → UAT PR; it never raises or merges that PR, and never edits UAT itself.
- **Releases** (`release_fileset.py`, `care_release.py`): a file-set generated by
  the deployment repo's own updater script from a transient
  `release_details.json` written outside the repo. Keep that JSON's shape
  exactly — extra inputs (target repo, JIRA) travel beside it, not in it.
- **BigQuery** (`release_queue.py`, `bq_cost.py`): INSERT only. Every cost
  statement passes `bq_guard.py`. An empty `BQ_DATASET` disables the queue
  cleanly; check `queue_enabled()` before reading.
- **Portal events** (`events_store.py`): the ONE writer/reader of the
  `portal_events` table (notifications, Auto-triage, deployment tracking) — a
  second append-only table under the same rules. Rows are flat and typed
  (`bigquery/portal_events.schema.json` + `_SCHEMA`, additive nullable columns
  only; a test fails when they differ); "read", "dismissed", "cleared" are new
  rows and every read is the latest row per subject. Reads bind every value as a
  query parameter. Nothing raises — an outage is `{"ok": False, "error"}` — and
  an empty `PORTAL_EVENTS_DATASET` is a per-process memory store.
- **Notifications** (`notifications.py`) sit on `events_store`: `notify` never
  raises or waits on the caller's work; a scope that already has a notification
  gets an `updated` row with the same subject; `mark` writes only the
  recipient's own subjects. A producer is one best-effort call at the place
  the fact is already known, wrapped so it can never fail or change the action
  it rides on (`pr_reconcile._notify_settled`, `promotion._notify_uat_pr`,
  `dataflow._follow_run` → `df_run.py`, `release_queue._notify_requeued`); the
  recipient is an email the code already has — the verified caller or the
  event's `requested_by` — never a typed one, and nobody known means nothing sent.
  A `df_run` watcher polls with the dispatch's session PAT, so it stops (silently)
  the moment the thread no longer holds it (`SessionCredentialStore.holds`) and
  never runs past `SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES`.
- **Tickets** (`tickets.py`): the CHG / RMG tickets named on a PR, found by a
  tokenizer (never regex) in the body then the comments oldest first — the
  newest mention per prefix wins, its state the last `TICKET_STATE_WORDS` word
  on its line. One GitHub read per (repo, PR) every ten minutes; a PR that
  cannot be read is `{"error"}`, never a raise. `note_first_seen` appends a
  `deploy`/`tickets` row only when something changed and rings the requester's
  bell only for a CHG id not seen before.
- **Support** (`tools/support/`): read-only L1 view of a control
  table. Generic ROLES only — the real table, columns, statuses and owners are
  config (`SUPPORT_*`; only `SUPPORT_TABLE` is required — `discover.py` maps the
  rest from the table's schema and status words), never code; the runbook is the plain-English skill
  `adk_release_agent/skills/support-runbook/SKILL.md` (parsed by `runbook.py`
  for the cards, read whole by the AI) — never a rule in code or a prompt. Its statements (`Query`: BigQuery counts, only problem rows come
  back) pass `bq_guard.run(..., allowed_tables=(table,))`;
  write it without CTEs (the guard would dry-run them). Error text reaches the
  model only with `SUPPORT_ERRORS_TO_MODEL` (`for_model`). It suggests actions;
  it never re-runs or changes a job.
  One module per job: mapping (`config.py`), statements (`queries.py`), the
  pure report (`report.py`), the L1 layer (`incidents.py`), each evidence reader
  on its own. An evidence read goes through `cache.remembered` keyed
  (kind, subject, business date) so the collector and the chat tools share it.
- **Auto-triage** (`support/watch.py`, preview feature `auto-triage`): findings
  are `events_store` rows (domain `watch`, subject `incident:<id>`, version =
  business date; long parts in `details`), never a table of their own; every
  change — cleared, resolved, dismissed, reopened, updated — is a NEW row. The
  finding's cause is what code established (`finding_from`, PURE); a timed-out
  investigation is a finding that says so. The bell goes through
  `notifications.notify` with one scope per incident; nothing here changes a job.
- **Parsing**: no regex. Split, partition and loop (see `json_splice.py`,
  `release_chain.py`).
